title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Gunnar Helm catches four passes in Week 1
items.desc: Gunnar Helm caught four of his five targets for 28 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Helm tied for second with four catches while finishing third on the team in receiving yards. The veteran tight end will be a TE3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Elic Ayomanor finds the end zone in Week 1
items.desc: Elic Ayomanor caught one of his three targets for an 11-yard touchdown in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Ayomanor was quiet for most of the afternoon until he pulled down his 11-yard touchdown in garbage time with 2:40 left in the game. The veteran wideout will be tough to trust as part of a below-average Tennessee passing attack going forward. The Titans will face the Eagles in Week 2.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Calvin Ridley not targeted in Week 1
items.desc: Calvin Ridley was not targeted in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Ridley was on the field but did not record any stats in the lopsided loss to New York. The entire Titans offense struggled in the contest, but Ridley's lack of participation is still highly concerning going forward. He can be cut in shallow leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Wan'Dale Robninson goes for 38 yards in Week 1
items.desc: Wan'Dale Robinson caught five of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Robinson tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while leading the way with his five catches. The entire Tennessee offense struggled to move the ball in Week 1, which cut into Robinson's final stats. He will look to bounce back as a decent flex option in PPR leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ravens D/ST stifles Colts in Week 1 win
items.desc: The Ravens D/ST recorded two sacks, one fumble recovery, and one interception in a Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: The defense stood tall in the season opener for first-year head coach Jesse Minter, allowing less than 275 offensive yards in the win. The unit will look to take advantage of a favorable Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Carnell Tate catches four passes in Week 1
items.desc: Carnell Tate caught four of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Tate tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while finishing second in receptions in his NFL debut. The rookie receiver will surely have bigger games going forward, as the entire Tennessee offense struggled in the season opener. Tate will be a low-end WR3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Tyjae Spears finishes with 24 all-purpose yards in Week 1
items.desc: Tyjae Spears carried the ball three times for 12 yards and caught two of his four targets for 12 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Spears operated behind Tony Pollard, who had eight touches. It was not a great day for the Tennessee run game, as the Titans were playing from behind for the entire game. Spears at least drew an encouraging number of targets in the passing attack. He will be a low-end flex option heading into Week 2 against the Eagles.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Tyler Loop racks up 11 points in Week 1 win
items.desc: Tyler Loop converted both of his field goal attempts as well as all five of his extra point attempts to finish with 11 points in a 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Loop capitalized on every opportunity for head coach Jesse Minter, finishing with a perfect stat line in the Week 1 win. The kicker will look to take advantage of another favorable matchup in Week 2 against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Tony Pollard held to 35 rushing yards in Week 1
items.desc: Tony Pollard carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and lost one yard on his lone catch in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Pollard was quiet with the Titans playing from behind for most of the game. On the bright side, the veteran running back led the backfield with Tyjae Spears getting just three carries. Pollard will look to bounce back as a high-end RB3 in Week 2 against the Eagles.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Derrick Henry rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Colts
items.desc: Derrick Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns while also hauling in his lone target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Henry capitalized on a sizeable workload out of the Baltimore backfield, averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry in the Week 1 win. The superstar running back remains locked in as a reliable RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Cam Ward struggles in Week 1 loss
items.desc: Cam Ward completed 19 of his 32 passes for 140 yards and a touchdown while adding 21 yards on four carries in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
items.impact: Ward struggled in the loss, averaging just 4.4 yards per attempt. His touchdown pass came in garbage time with the game out of reach on an 11-yard catch from Elic Ayomanor. Ward will be a low-end QB2 heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Eagles.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Lamar Jackson surpasses 300 passing yards in Week 1 win over Colts
items.desc: Lamar Jackson completed 17-of-25 pass attempts for 324 yards and one touchdown while also rushing seven times for 40 yards, one touchdown, and one lost fumble in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Jackson took advantage of a more explosive offensive playbook from first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, accounting for touchdowns on the ground and through the air in the win. The superstar quarterback remains an elite QB1 option entering a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Jets D/ST holds Titans to 10 points
items.desc: The Jets D/ST allowed 10 points while forcing one turnover and notching three sacks in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: The Jets' defenders made it a difficult afternoon for Cam Ward and company in the season opener. They recovered a Chimere Dike for their turnover while Kingsley Enagbare, Will McDonald IV, and David Bailey each had a sack. Things will be much tougher for this unit in Week 2 against the Packers.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Jason Sanders hits three FGs in Week 1
items.desc: Jason Sanders made three of his four field goals and added two extra points in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: Sanders showed off his big leg, hitting two 50-yard field goals in the win. The veteran kicker didn't kick in the 2025 season but he prevailed as the Jets' top option after winning the job in the preseason. He will look to stay hot in Week 2's home matchup against the Packers.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Kenyon Sadiq rushes for TD in Week 1
items.desc: Kenyon Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 21 yards and added a three-yard rushing touchdown in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 2.
items.impact: Sadiq turned in a quiet outing in the passing attack but he scored the Jets' first TD of the season on his three-yard carry in the first quarter. The team's willingness to use the first-round rookie in the running game is an encouraging development for his fantasy value moving forward. Sadiq will be a solid TE2 in Week 2 against the Packers.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Adonai Mitchell goes for 60 yards in Week 1
items.desc: Adonai Mitchell caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: Mitchell finished second on the Jets in receiving yards, operating as the team's deep threat. He did most of his damage on a 40-yard pass from Geno Smith. While Mitchell will remain behind Garrett Wilson in the target pecking order, he has some boom/bust potential in a Jets offense that looked much improved from last year. Mitchell settles in as a flex option in Week 2 against Green Bay.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Garrett Wilson goes for 79 yards in Week 1
items.desc: Garrett Wilson caught six of his seven targets for 79 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: Wilson led the Jets in all receiving categories in the easy win over an overmatched Tennessee team. Even though it wasn't a huge performance from Wilson, it was an encouraging debut for the receiver with Geno Smith at the helm. Wilson settles in as a high-end WR2 in a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Braelon Allen sees 10 carres in backup role in Week 1
items.desc: Braelon Allen carried the ball 10 times for 40 yards and failed to corral his lone target in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: Allen mixed in as the backup behind Breece Hall, who handled 22 carries and caught two passes. The Jets will continue to utilize Allen to spell Hall throughout the season, but the former only has fantasy value as a handcuff for the time being. He will take on the Packers at home in Week 2.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Breece Hall finds the end zone in Week 1 win
items.desc: Breece Hall carried the ball 22 times for 102 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 16 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: Hall dealt with a groin issue during camp, but he appeared to be at full health in the Week 1 win. The veteran running back handled the majority of the backfield carries, with Braelon Allen mixing in for 10 totes. Hall found the end zone for the first time of the season on a four-yard rush in the third quarter. He will slot in as a solid RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Geno Smith solid in Week 1 win over Titans
items.desc: Geno Smith completed 19 of his 24 passes for 215 yards while adding seven yards on six carries in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
items.impact: It was a solid outing for the veteran quarterback in his return to the Jets. Smith did not throw any touchdowns in the win, but he also didn't turn the ball over and kept the chains moving. Smith will look to keep rolling as a low-end QB2 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Mark Andrews sees six targets in Week 1 win
items.desc: Mark Andrews hauled in four of his six targets for 49 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Andrews received sizeable volume in the Baltimore passing attack, finishing tied for first in targets in the win. The veteran tight end remains a reliable option ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Chris Moore catches one pass in Week 1
items.desc: Chris Moore caught one of his two targets for 53 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
items.impact: Moore made up for an otherwise forgettable day with an explosive play in the Week 1 win. The veteran wideout could be in line for increased targets after both Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) exited with injuries in the season opener, with a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: LaJohntay Webster catches two passes in Week 1
items.desc: LaJohntay Webster caught both of his targets for 15 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
items.impact: Webster saw minimal usage in the Baltimore passing attack, finishing tied for third in targets in the win. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Matt Hibner catches one pass in Week 1
items.desc: Matt Hibner caught his only target for 13 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
items.impact: Hibner joined Durham Smythe in finishing behind veteran Mark Andrews in tight end targets in the win. The rookie can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Justice Hill sees seven touches in Week 1
items.desc: Justice Hill rushed six times for 18 yards while catching his only target for 10 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
items.impact: Hill operated as more of an afterthought out of the Baltimore backfield, with Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson finishing ahead of the running back in carries. He remains more of a change-of-pace option behind Henry ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Durham Smythe catches only target in Week 1
items.desc: Durham Smythe caught his only target for four yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Smythe saw minimal usage in the Week 1 win, joining rookie Matthew Hibner in finishing behind veteran Mark Andrews in tight end targets in the win. The tight end remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Rashod Bateman sees one target in Week 1
items.desc: Rashod Bateman failed to catch his lone target in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
items.impact: Bateman operated as more of an afterthought in a Baltimore passing attack that lost both Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) to injury, but could be in line for increased usage if either of the pass-catchers misses time ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Kyler Murray (concussion) ruled out Sunday
items.desc: Kyler Murray (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 1 for the Minnesota Vikings against the Green Bay Packers according to Adam Schefter.
items.impact: Murray suffered the apparent concussion in the first quarter after being hit by Green Bay safety Jevon Bullard, with backup Carson Wentz taking over behind center for head coach Kevin O'Connell.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
items.desc: Zay Flowers (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 1 contest between the Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts according to Mike Garafolo.
items.impact: Flowers had been sidelined since the second quarter while attempting to work through the hamstring injury an return for head coach Jesse Minter, hauling in five of his six targets for 150 receiving yards and one touchdown on the day.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) ruled out Sunday
items.desc: Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) has been ruled out for the Baltimore Ravens against the Indianapolis Colts according to Ian Rapoport.
items.impact: Lane joins fellow wideout Zay Flowers (hamstring) on the sidelines for new head coach Jesse Minter, catching one of his three targets for 11 receiving yards prior to exiting. Rashod Bateman should command even more targets in the second half from quarterback Lamar Jackson in Week 1.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) ruled out with an ankle injury jury
items.desc: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Jets game against the Titans.
items.impact: Cooper had a nice 30 yard snag in this game, but was taken off the field on a cart. Fantasy managers will need to monitor his situation as details come through.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Aaron Banks (knee) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Aaron Banks (knee) is inactive for Week 1 for the Green Bay Packers against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Banks will not suit up after being unable to progress through pregame activities for the Packers, leaving the offensive line shorthanded for the Week 1 divisional matchup.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) active for Week 1
items.desc: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is active for Week 1 for the Arizona Cardinals against the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Love is good to go after clearing through pregame activities without any setbacks from the injured ankle, with the rookie running back set to share the backfield with free agent Tyler Allgeier against the Chargers.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) questionable to return
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is questionable to return for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: Thomas Jr. suffered the apparent shoulder injury in the second quarter of the Week 1 contest, hauling in all three of his targets for 40 yards prior to exiting.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Christian Mahogany (knee) questionable to return
items.desc: Christian Mahogany (knee) is questionable to return to the Detroit Lions Sunday the organization announced.
items.impact: Mahogany suffered the knee injury early in the first quarter of the Week 1 contest, with Ben Bartch taking over at left guard for head coach Dan Campbell against the Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) active for Week 1
items.desc: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) is active for Week 1 for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: Allen Jr. passed through pregame activities without any issues and will join a Jacksonville backfield led by Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. for head coach Liam Cohen against the Browns Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (leg) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (leg) is inactive for Week 1 for the Detroit Lions against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Rakestraw Jr. will not suit while continuing to work through a lingering leg injury, leaving the Detroit secondary without another key option for head coach Dan Campbell against the Saints Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Derrick Moore (hamstring) active for Week 1
items.desc: Derrick Moore (hamstring) is active for Week 1 for the Detroit Lions against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Moore is good to go after clearing through pregame activities without any issues, offering a boost to a Detroit front seven that will look to disrupt the New Orleans offense on a consistent basis Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jalen McMillan (knee) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Jalen McMillan (knee) is inactive for Week 1 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cincinnati Bengals.
items.impact: McMillan will not suit up after being unable to clear through pregame activities due to the lingering knee injury, with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr, and Ted Hurst III to lead the Tampa Bay pass-catching group against the Bengals for head coach Todd Bowles.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Sean Tucker (hamstring) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Sean Tucker (hamstring) is inactive for Week 1 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cincinnati Bengals.
items.impact: Tucker will be sidelined for the season opener after being unable to clear through pregame activities for head coach Todd Bowles. Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell will lead the Tampa Bay backfield attack against a revamped Bengals defense Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Devontez Walker (groin) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Devontez Walker (groin) is inactive for Week 1 for the Baltimore Ravens against the Indianapolis Colts according to Jamison Hensley.
items.impact: Walker will not suit up after testing his injured groin during pregame activities for head coach Jesse Minter, with superstar Zay Flowers and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane to lead the Baltimore wideout group against the Colts in Week 1.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Cooper Rush (back) active for Week 1
items.desc: Cooper Rush (back) is active for Week 1 for the Atlanta Falcons against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
items.impact: Rush is good to go and will start behind center for new head coach Kevin Stefanski after experiencing back spasms Saturday. The veteran signal-caller will look to survive against an aggressive Pittsburgh defensive front, with running back Bijan Robinson, wideout Drake London, and tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. to be relied on heavily Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Alvin Kamara (knee) inactive for Week 1
items.desc: Alvin Kamara (knee) is inactive for Week 1 for the New Orleans Saints against the Detroit Lions according to Nick Underhill.
items.impact: Kamara will sit out the season opener while continuing to work through a knee injury for head coach Kellen Moore, with Travis Etienne Jr. to lead the New Orleans backfield attack and Kendre Miller to also receive touches against the Lions.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Rome Odunze (calf) active for Week 1
items.desc: Rome Odunze (calf) is officially active for Week 1 for the Chicago Bears against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Odunze is good to go after passing through pregame testing without any setbacks from the calf injury, offering head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catching option for quarterback Caleb Williams against the Panthers Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Myles Garrett (knee) to undergo surgery, placed on injured reserve
items.desc: Myles Garrett (knee) will undergo arthroscopic surgery and will be placed on injured reserve by the Los Angeles Rams according to Tom Pelissero.
items.impact: Garrett was stifled in Thursday night's season opener while still being limited with the knee injury for head coach Sean McVay and will now miss at least the next four games.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) on snap count for Week 1
items.desc: Alec Pierce (heel) will operate on a snap count in Week 1 for the Indianapolis Colts against the Baltimore Ravens according to Mike Garafolo.
items.impact: Pierce is in line for 20-60 plays according to Garafolo as the wideout continues to work back towards full health after a late start to his preseason activities for the Colts. Tight end Tyler Warren alongside wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs will likely see increased targets from quarterback Daniel Jones against the Ravens Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Malik Nabers (knee) game-time decision for Week 1
items.desc: Malik Nabers (knee) will be a game-time decision for the Week 1 contest between the New York Giants against the Dallas Cowboys Sunday night according to Adam Schefter.
items.impact: Nabers continues to work back from a severe knee injury suffered during the 2025-26 season and could potentially leave head coach John Harbaugh without his top pass-catching option in a key Week 1 divisional matchup. Fantasy managers will need to have another option ready to plug into lineups whether it be in one of the earlier kickoff windows Sunday or an available option in the Monday night contest between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos.
